guideTitle: The Best Gaming Chairs for Tall People, Compared by Backrest Height
breadcrumbLabel: Best Gaming Chairs for Tall People
metaTitle: Best Gaming Chairs for Tall People: Backrest Height (2026)
metaDescription: For tall users, backrest height and headrest position matter more than weight rating. We compared eight gaming chairs with 46- to 53-inch backs on height, recline and fit.
introParagraphs: A gaming chair for a tall person isn't necessarily a big and tall chair. Big and tall models are built around weight capacity and width; a tall user of average build mainly needs a backrest high enough to support the shoulders and a headrest that can sit behind the neck rather than the upper back.

The eight chairs below list backrest heights from about 46 to 53 inches. Check that figure against your seated shoulder height, then consider the headrest, recline range and seat height. Weight ratings range from 300 to 400 lb; choose the higher ratings only if you need them.
Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing. Manufacturers measure backrest height differently, so treat small differences with caution.

gtplayer-saddle-400-matte-black.summary: A 400 lb-rated wingback chair with a 3D saddle cushion, dual-spring lumbar and footrest.
gtplayer-saddle-400-matte-black.description:
This big and tall chair is the established choice here, with an extensive and positive base of buyer feedback. Its high wingback extends further up the back than a standard high-back chair, and it pairs a dual-spring lumbar with a 3D saddle cushion designed to spread weight.

It reclines from 90 to 150 degrees, has height-adjustable armrests and a pull-out footrest, and is rated for 400 lb.

The listing doesn't give a backrest height, so compare it directly with the chairs that do, and the big-and-tall frame is bulkier than a tall user of average build may need.
cons: Costs more than several taller-backed chairs
gtplayer-saddle-400-matte-black.bestFor: Tall and heavier users who want a proven chair with built-in lumbar.
gtplayer-saddle-400-matte-black.skipIf: You want a stated backrest height; the LEMBERI lists 52.9 inches for much less.

homall-highback-478-white.summary: A 47.8-inch high-back racing chair with a 155-degree recline, at the lowest price here.
homall-highback-478-white.description:
The Homall gives a 47.8-inch backrest for the lowest price here at the time of writing, and it is one of the most widely bought gaming chairs.

It has a 1.8mm steel frame, a 90- to 155-degree recline, and removable headrest and lumbar pillows you can position yourself. Homall rates its casters for 1,000 miles, and the chair for 300 lb.

It is PU leather, which can feel warm, and it has no footrest listed.
pros: Tall back at the lowest price here
homall-highback-478-white.bestFor: Tall users of average build on a budget.
homall-highback-478-white.skipIf: You need more height; the LEMBERI's back is 52.9 inches.

lemberi-529-red-footrest.summary: The tallest backrest here at 52.9 inches, with footrest, massage lumbar and Class 4 gas lift.
lemberi-529-red-footrest.description:
The LEMBERI has the tallest backrest in this guide, 52.9 inches, about five inches more than the Homall, which makes it the first chair to check if your head clears the top of standard chairs.

It has a massage lumbar pillow, headrest, linkage armrests, a 90- to 155-degree recline, a footrest and a Class 4 gas lift, and is rated for 400 lb. It was under $100 at the time of writing.

The red finish won't suit every room, and the massage pillow adds a cable.
lemberi-529-red-footrest.bestFor: The tallest users, where backrest height is the priority.
lemberi-529-red-footrest.skipIf: You prefer fabric; the GTPLAYER Leatheraire has a 51-inch back in fabric.

ngen-highback-465-carbon.summary: A 46.5-inch high-back chair with a steel frame, SGS-rated gas lift and pull-out footrest.
ngen-highback-465-carbon.description:
The N-GEN High Back gives tall users a footrest and a 46.5-inch back at a low price, with a stainless steel frame and SGS-rated gas lift. Buyer feedback is very positive.

Its detachable headrest and lower-back pillow can be positioned to suit you, and it is rated for 300 lb.

At 46.5 inches, its back is among the shorter here, so very tall users may prefer the LEMBERI or GTPLAYER Leatheraire.
ngen-highback-465-carbon.bestFor: Moderately tall users who want a footrest for less.
ngen-highback-465-carbon.skipIf: You're very tall; the LEMBERI's back is over six inches taller.

gtplayer-leatheraire-51-black.summary: A 51-inch back in breathable Leatheraire fabric, with pocket-spring cushion and linkage armrests.
gtplayer-leatheraire-51-black.description:
The GTPLAYER Leatheraire pairs a 51-inch back, second only to the LEMBERI, with fabric GTPLAYER rates as twice as breathable as standard PU, which may help with a full-length backrest in a warm room.

It has a pocket-spring cushion, self-adjusting linkage armrests, an FSC-certified frame and butterfly embroidery, and is rated for 300 lb.

It has no footrest.
gtplayer-leatheraire-51-black.bestFor: Tall users who run warm and prefer fabric.
gtplayer-leatheraire-51-black.skipIf: You want a footrest; the LEMBERI has one with an even taller back.

ngen-bigtall-4606-dark-black.badge: Tall and Heavy Build for Less
ngen-bigtall-4606-dark-black.summary: A 400 lb-rated chair with a 46.06-inch back, pocket-spring cushion and footrest.
ngen-bigtall-4606-dark-black.description:
The N-GEN Big & Tall combines a 400 lb rating with a 46.06-inch back, a pocket-spring cushion, linked armrests and a footrest, under $100 at the time of writing.

It uses reinforced steel.

Its back is the shortest here, its 135-degree recline is the shallowest, and buyer feedback is limited so far. The LEMBERI offers a taller back and a 400 lb rating for a similar price.
ngen-bigtall-4606-dark-black.bestFor: Moderately tall, heavier users who want a soft seat.
ngen-bigtall-4606-dark-black.skipIf: Backrest height matters most; the LEMBERI is taller at a similar price.

vitesse-bigtall-4744-footrest.summary: A 47.44-inch back with an oversized memory foam headrest, 155-degree recline and 400 lb rating.
vitesse-bigtall-4744-footrest.description:
The VITESSE focuses on neck support: its oversized memory foam headrest is larger than the pillows on most chairs here, paired with a memory foam lumbar cushion, on a 47.44-inch back.

It has linkage armrests, a 90- to 155-degree recline, a footrest, an FSC steel frame and SGS-rated gas lift, and is rated for 400 lb.

It costs more than the LEMBERI, which has a taller back, at the time of writing.
cons: Less buyer feedback than the top picks
vitesse-bigtall-4744-footrest.bestFor: Tall users whose main complaint is neck support.
vitesse-bigtall-4744-footrest.skipIf: Backrest height is the priority; the LEMBERI is taller for less.

homrelexa-flip-armrest-483.summary: A 48.3-inch back with flip armrests that widen the seat area from 22.8 to 38.6 inches.
homrelexa-flip-armrest-483.description:
The HOMRELEXA pairs a 48.3-inch back with flip-up armrests that widen the usable seat area from 22.8 to 38.6 inches, useful if you like to shift position or sit cross-legged.

It has soft teddy fabric over a coil layer, two recline modes HOMRELEXA calls Focus and Chill, a footrest and a 400 lb rating.

It was the most expensive chair here at the time of writing, and the width is a comfort feature rather than a height-fit one.
cons: Most expensive here at the time of writing
homrelexa-flip-armrest-483.bestFor: Tall users who want room to move in the seat.
homrelexa-flip-armrest-483.skipIf: Height is all you need; the LEMBERI is taller for less than half the price.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Listed heights here run from 46.06 inches (N-GEN Big & Tall) to 52.9 inches (LEMBERI). Measure from the seat to the top of your shoulders when seated and choose a back that clears it.
A headrest pillow you can move, or a large one like the VITESSE's, is more likely to sit behind your neck.
Weight rating and height fit are separate. If you're tall but not heavy, a 300 lb chair with a tall back may suit you as well as a 400 lb model.
Recline runs from 135 to 155 degrees here; several chairs add footrests.

faq.q: How is a chair for tall people different from big and tall?
faq.a: Big and tall chairs prioritize weight capacity and width. Tall users mainly need backrest height and headrest reach. Some chairs, like the LEMBERI, offer both.

faq.q: How tall should the backrest be?
faq.a: Tall enough to clear your shoulders when seated. Measure seat-to-shoulder height and compare it with the listed backrest heights, which range from about 46 to 53 inches here.

faq.q: Do I need a 400 lb rating if I'm tall but not heavy?
faq.a: No. Choose based on backrest height and headrest; the Homall and GTPLAYER Leatheraire are rated for 300 lb.
It matters for lounging. The Homall, LEMBERI and VITESSE reach 155 degrees; the N-GEN Big & Tall stops at 135.
Only if you want room to shift position. They don't affect height fit.

bottomLine: For the tallest users, the LEMBERI's 52.9-inch back is the first to consider, and it costs under $100 at the time of writing. The GTPLAYER Leatheraire offers 51 inches in breathable fabric, and the Homall 47.8 inches for the least money.

If neck support is the issue, the VITESSE's large headrest is the better fit; for a proven chair that also suits a heavier build, the GTPLAYER Saddle is the established option. The HOMRELEXA adds seat width at a higher price.
